title: Protocol for construction and characterization of direct electron transfer-based enzyme-electrode using gold binding peptide as molecular binder
protocol: Transform expression plasmid into Escherichia coli BL21-Rosetta (DE3) with heat shock method.
Plate transformed cells on LB agar plates containing 100 μg/mL of ampicillin and incubate at 37°C for 14–16 hours.
Pick a single colony from the LB-ampicillin plate and inoculate a starter culture of 5 mL LB-ampicillin medium, then incubate at 37°C for 8 hours.
Inoculate Terrific Broth (TB) medium containing 100 μg/mL ampicillin with the starter culture at a 1:50 dilution.
Culture Escherichia coli BL21-Rosetta (DE3) harboring target gene plasmid in 500 mL TB medium with 100 μg/mL ampicillin in a 1 L flask at 37°C until OD600 reaches 0.6.
Add IPTG to the culture to a final concentration of 0.2 mM and incubate at 16°C for 18 hours.
Harvest cells by centrifugation at 3,500 g and 4°C for 20 minutes.
Mix harvested cells with 15 mL Buffer A50 (pH 7.4).
Disrupt resuspended cells using sonication cycles of 2 seconds ON and 4 seconds OFF at 40% amplitude to ensure complete cell lysis.
Centrifuge the lysates at 13,000 g and 4°C for 30 minutes.
Collect the supernatant.
Filter the supernatant through a 0.45-μm syringe filter to remove cell debris and inclusion bodies.
Equilibrate filtered soluble fractions with Ni-NTA agarose resin by rotating end-to-end at 40 rpm.
Wash the column with Buffer A50 of 10 column volumes.
Pass two column volumes each of Buffer A70, Buffer A350, and Buffer A500 through the nickel column sequentially.
Exchange the protein-containing buffer with PBS using an Amicon Ultra-15 30K filter centrifugal filter.
Select a molecular weight cut-off close to one-third the target protein size.
Cleave the his-tag by treating with TEV protease at 30°C for 2 hours.
Estimate the protein concentration by Bradford assay.
Adjust the protein concentration to 0.33 μg/μL in a total volume of 45 μL.
Add 5 μL of TEV Protease Reaction Buffer (10×).
Add 1 μL of TEV Protease (10 U).
Incubate at 30°C for 2 hours.
Conform the cleavage of his-tag on a 10% SDS-PAGE gel.
Filter the protein mixture through an Amicon Ultra-15 30K filter to remove or minimize cleaved his-tag and TEV protease contents.
Prepare 60 μL DCIP mixture in 96-well plate at 25°C.
Add 20 μL purified enzyme (0.05 mg/mL) and incubate at 25°C for 3 min without stirring.
Add 20 μL of 2 M glucose to initiate glucose oxidation, or add 20 μL deionized water to perform blank at OD600.
After 1 minute, stop the reaction by adding 100 μL of 6 M urea.
Measure absorbance at OD600.
Calculate enzyme activity based on the Beer-Lambert Law.
Prepare 100 mL of 1:3 (v/v) 30% H2O2/H2SO4 piranha solution in a 500 mL beaker.
Incubate the gold substrate in the piranha solution for 10 min at 25°C.
Rinse the gold substrate with deionized water and dry it with pressurized nitrogen gas.
Add 500 μL of 0.1 μM target enzyme dissolved in PBS (pH 7.4) into a 1.5 mL microtube.
Insert the surface-cleaned gold substrate into the enzyme solution-containing microtube.
Incubate the gold substrate with the enzyme solution on a rotary shaker at 200 rpm for 2 h at 25°C.
Remove weakly bound proteins from the gold surface by sonication (30 Hz) in enzyme-free PBS for 30 s.
Wash off salts from the protein-bound gold surface with a stream of deionized water for 30 s.
Dry the protein-bound gold surface with 99.9% nitrogen gas.
Measure the surface morphology of the protein-bound gold surface using AFM in non-contact mode.
Fix the protein-bound gold substrate on the sample stage of the AFM instrument (XE-100; Park Systems, Langen, Germany).
Install the 125-μm Si/Al-coated cantilevers with 200–400-kHz resonance frequency and 42 N/m spring constant.
Align the cantilever on the center of sample surface.
Image the surface morphology in  1 μm × 1 μm scan fields, at 1 Hz scan rate.
Process the raw AFM image with XEI software to remove undesired artifacts such as slope and curvature using the 1st order fitting curve.
Dry the enzyme-bound specimen completely before imaging to prevent vertical drift caused by water molecules.
Conduct cyclic voltammetry (CV) timing from 2–8 hours to measure interfacial electron transfer rate between enzymatic cofactor and electrode surface.
Analyze onset potential in CV to identify presence of direct electron transfer signal.
Measure peak current in the cyclic voltammogram to assess interfacial direct electron transfer efficiency.
Prepare screen-printed gold electrode (SPGE) consisting of Au working electrode, Pt auxiliary electrode, and Ag pseudo-reference electrode.
Verify that the SPGE does not have interfering electrochemical signals by conducting CV with a bare SPGE.
Add 800 μL of 0.5 μM target enzyme dissolved in PBS buffer (pH 7.4) to a disposable cuvette.
Immerse the SPGE into the cuvette containing the enzyme solution and incubate it on a rotary shaker at 200 rpm for 2 hours at 25°C.
Wash off excess proteins from the gold working electrode surfaces with a stream of PBS for 30 seconds.
Connect the enzyme-modified SPGE to a potentiostat (Autolab, Metrohm).
Immerse the enzyme-modified SPGE in a reactor containing 8 mL of 10 mM potassium phosphate buffer (pH 7.4) and adjust the working volume to 10 mL.
Add 2 M glucose stock dissolved in 10 mM potassium-based phosphate buffer (pH 7.4) to achieve a glucose content ranging from 0 to 100 mM for detection.
Set the scan rate to 100 mV/s and perform CV in the potential range of -500 mV to 400 mV using Nova 1.11 program.
Continue cycling until the signal stabilizes, which typically occurs after 20-30 cycles.
Change the scan direction to reverse and observe that there is no large difference in the signal compared to the original direction.
